items.title: Blood Moon
items.author: Britney S. Lewis
items.synopsis_full: The Instant #1 New York Times Bestseller Mirabella Owens grew up with legends of wolves that traveled to her midwestern town to protect humans from vampires. Of a werewolf that fell in love with one of the undead, unraveling a blood-soaked history. But Mira stopped believing in those fairy tales years ago. She stopped believing in a lot of things after her mom left without a trace when she was only thirteen. As Mira begins her freshman year at Lakeland University, she’s ready to leave the past behind her. Only the past isn’t finished with her yet. Strange animal attacks are occurring around campus, reopening cold cases tied to her mother’s disappearance. And the only person who seems to know anything is Julian Santos, the boy who is hell-bent on getting Mira to leave campus for reasons she can’t begin to understand. But Mira refuses to let him keep his secrets, not when the truth is the difference between life and death. Mira will have to accept that there is much more to the old town myths, and her growing feelings for Julian, than she ever could have anticipated. And as the Blood Moon rises, she will come to know a world that will shatter her past and change her future.

items.title: Falling Like Snow
items.author: Misty Wilson
items.synopsis_short: A girl juggles planning her town’s…
items.synopsis_full: A girl juggles planning her town’s first-ever winter festival and untangling her complicated feelings for both her best friend and the star hockey player in this charming book in the swoony Bramble Falls series that started with the New York Times bestselling Falling Like Leaves. After Bramble Falls’s wildly successful Falling Leaves Festival, Sloane Sullivan is looking forward to some downtime—especially kicking back and marathoning Nora Ephron movies with her best friend, Asher. But they barely make it through Sleepless in Seattle before Sloane’s mom calls an emergency tourism department meeting; it’s all hands on deck—Bramble Falls is having its first ever Falling Snow Festival! Sloane may still be recovering from the last seasonal event, but she’s also excited. After all, Christmas is the best time of year! And she’ll have her whole crew by her side, including her cousin Ellis and, of course, Asher. But when irresistible, hockey-playing Micah catches Sloane’s attention, she finds herself a bit distracted. The emotions her unexpected flirtation brings up make Sloane feel confused about Micah…and Asher. She’s never thought of Asher as more than her best friend, but even if Sloane is seeing Asher in a new light, what does that mean for her and Micah? Uncertain and more than a little overwhelmed, Sloane throws herself into festival preparations, hoping to get a little Christmas magic in return that will help her figure out where her heart lies.

items.title: The Stones Cry Out
items.author: Dinesh D'Souza
items.synopsis_short: What can ancient evidence really tell…
items.synopsis_full: What can ancient evidence really tell us about Scripture, and where should careful readers draw the line between discovery, interpretation, faith, and prophecy? Lessons from The Stones Cry Out by Dinesh D’Souza is an independently created lessons and insights resource for readers who want to think more carefully about biblical archaeology and the historical world behind Scripture. Rather than retelling the original book, Janet B. Ritter develops practical principles for evaluating archaeological claims, understanding chronology and context, comparing written and material evidence, and approaching disputed questions with intellectual discipline. Inside this book, readers will explore how geography, inscriptions, ruins, destruction layers, imperial records, and ancient cities can illuminate the biblical world; why evidence and interpretation must remain distinct; how archaeology can strengthen historical understanding without being asked to prove theological claims it cannot establish; how questions surrounding Israel, Jerusalem, the Temple, and prophecy require careful attention to both history and interpretation; and how faith can engage evidence without depending on exaggeration or sensational conclusions. The result is a thoughtful framework for readers who want to appreciate the significance of ancient discoveries while remaining alert to uncertainty, competing interpretations, and the limits of what archaeology can demonstrate. It also considers what responsible study of the past may teach us about reading prophetic claims concerning the future. Disclaimer: This book is an independently created lessons and insights resource related to the main book. It is not the original book and is not written by, endorsed by, sponsored by, or affiliated with Dinesh D’Souza or the publisher of the original work.
